The mathematics is the theory of Cartan subgroups of smooth group schemes over a base S, the material of SGA 3 Exp. XIII.
- Setup: G is a smooth S-group scheme. 𝒞 is the scheme of Cartan subgroups. X ⊂ G_𝒞 is the universal Cartan subgroup, and ψ: X → G is the composite X → G_𝒞 → G. U ⊂ G is the open set of regular points (regular in their fibre), defined as G_b with b the section of 2.7.
- To define b, one splits S into the open and closed pieces S_{n,ρ}, on which G has relative dimension n and nilpotent rank ρ.
- Theorem 3.1: ψ^{-1}(U) → U is an isomorphism, and U is the largest open subset with this property.
- Proof: ψ^{-1}(U) and U are smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, so the fibrewise criterion applies. This reduces to S = Spec of an algebraically closed field. There, by the conjugacy theorem, 𝒞 ≅ G/N with N the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup C, and ψ becomes the map G ×^N C → G of No. 2; one concludes by 2.6 b).
- Corollary 3.2: a regular section g of G lies in exactly one Cartan subgroup. This is just a restatement of the isomorphism over U.
- The last paragraph identifies ψ^{-1}(U) with the open set of points of X that are regular in G_𝒞.

This is published material (SGA 3) and has nothing to do with the cycle-theoretic content of the surrounding folder. The next page returns to blow-ups and Chow groups.

ideas.what: Over the regular locus, the map from the universal Cartan subgroup to G is an isomorphism, and the regular locus is the largest open set with this property. Proved by the fibrewise isomorphism criterion plus conjugacy of Cartan subgroups over algebraically closed fields.
ideas.modern_name: Universal Cartan subgroup / Grothendieck–Springer-type map G×^N C → G, isomorphism over regular elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 3, Exp. XIII), building on Chevalley
ideas.where_published: SGA 3, Exposé XIII (Sous-groupes de Cartan, éléments réguliers)

ideas.what: A regular section of a smooth group scheme lies in a unique Cartan subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: Unique Cartan subgroup containing a regular section
